panels.title: Read this before the numbers below

options.content:
**The bottom row is this repository's own, and is the only part of this page that is stable by construction (gh#536).** `MarqSpec.Mcp.TopstepX` is a `Meter` and an `ActivitySource` named by this repository, so its instrument names and tag values change only when this repository changes them — which [ADR-0019](../../documentation/adr/0019-otlp-as-the-telemetry-boundary.md) decision 6 says is where a panel that must not break belongs. Its tag values come from closed vocabularies (`series`, `outcome`, `operation`, `reason`, `transition`, `change`) plus an instrument symbol and a resolution. The vocabularies are closed and a unit test enumerates them, refusing a timestamp, a contract id or vendor free text; `resolution` is not closed but is bounded — `ToolGuards.ValidateResolution` refuses anything outside 1..1379, so the tag set is finite by construction.

**Every panel ABOVE that row except "Npgsql query duration" reads a metric the .NET SDK's `Experimental.ModelContextProtocol` `ActivitySource`/`Meter`, ASP.NET Core, HttpClient or the .NET runtime emits on its own — none of them are this repository's own instrumentation (that is gh#536).** The `Experimental` name is the vendor's, not a hedge added here: [ADR-0019](../../documentation/adr/0019-otlp-as-the-telemetry-boundary.md) records that an SDK bump may rename or drop these, and a broken panel after upgrading `ModelContextProtocol.Core` is that risk landing, not a regression in this dashboard. Verified against a real `grafana/otel-lgtm:0.32.1` container receiving real OTLP from this server (gh#535): the instrument is `mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds` (a histogram, Prometheus's translation of the OTLP name `mcp.server.operation.duration`), labelled `mcp_method_name` (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, ...), and — on a `tools/call` span only — `gen_ai_tool_name` (the tool actually invoked, e.g. `get_market_session`) and `error_type` (present only when the call failed).

**"Npgsql query duration" reads Npgsql's own meter.** `Npgsql` 10.0.3 ships the histogram `db.client.operation.duration` (`Npgsql.MeterProviderBuilderExtensions.AddNpgsqlInstrumentation`, subscribed by `ConfigureTelemetry` in `Program.cs`), and this panel reads its Prometheus translation, `db_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket`. Measured against a real `grafana/otel-lgtm:0.32.1` container (gh#553): after one store-reading tool call, `db_client_operation_duration_seconds_count{service_name="marqspec-mcp-topstepx", db_system_name="postgresql"}` read `2`, labelled `server_address="postgres"` and `db_client_connection_pool_name`. This is the SDK-owned instrument the note above already covers — a Npgsql bump could still rename or drop it — not a second, independent instability from a Tempo-derived metric.

**"Venue HttpClient latency" excludes `server_address="lgtm"` on purpose.** The OTLP **gRPC** exporter used here runs over `Grpc.Net.Client`, which is itself an `HttpClient` — so this server's own spans-and-metrics export traffic to the collector shows up in the *same* `http_client_request_duration_seconds` histogram as a real ProjectX call, tagged with the collector's own address and port. Left in, the panel would mostly show this container talking to itself. Measured on this branch with no ProjectX credentials configured, so nothing here separately confirms a *venue* call reaches the panel once one exists.

**Trace → log click-through**: this image provisions Loki's `trace_id` field as a Tempo-linked derived field out of the box (`docker/grafana-datasources.yaml` in `grafana/docker-otel-lgtm`), so every log line's trace id in Explore is already a link. This profile publishes only Grafana, on `127.0.0.1:3000`; Tempo's and Loki's own ports are reachable only from the `server` container, over the compose network. To reproduce the click-through by hand from the host, go through Grafana's own datasource proxy on that one port rather than Tempo's or Loki's — see README.md's "See what it is doing" for the runnable `curl` pair (verified end to end on gh#553: one `tools/call` produced a span in Tempo and, in the same second, a log line in Loki carrying the identical trace id).

panels.title: Tool-call latency by mcp.method.name (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Experimental.ModelContextProtocol's mcp.server.operation.duration histogram (Prometheus name mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds), one line per mcp.method.name. Unstable SDK-owned instrument name -- see the note panel above.

panels.title: Tool-call rate and error rate
panels.description: Rate of mcp_server_operation_duration_seconds_count by mcp.method.name (calls/sec), and the subset carrying an error.type attribute (a failed tools/call). Same unstable SDK instrument as the latency panel.

panels.title: Venue HttpClient latency (p95)
panels.description: OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http's http.client.request.duration (Prometheus name http_client_request_duration_seconds), by server.address -- the ProjectX venue and anything else this process reaches over HttpClient. server_address="lgtm" is excluded: the OTLP gRPC exporter here is itself an HttpClient and would otherwise show this container's own export traffic as if it were a venue call. Unstable SDK instrument name, same caveat as the panels above.

panels.title: Npgsql query duration (p95)
panels.description: Npgsql's own db.client.operation.duration histogram (Prometheus name db_client_operation_duration_seconds), subscribed by ConfigureTelemetry's AddNpgsqlInstrumentation. Same unstable-on-a-dependency-bump caveat as the SDK-meter panels above -- this one on Npgsql rather than ModelContextProtocol.Core -- but it is a real Npgsql meter, not a Tempo-derived span metric.

panels.title: Process memory (working set)
panels.description: The .NET runtime instrumentation's process.memory.usage (Prometheus name dotnet_process_memory_working_set_bytes).

panels.title: GC collections by generation
panels.description: The .NET runtime instrumentation's dotnet.gc.collections (Prometheus name dotnet_gc_collections_total), rate per generation.

panels.title: This repository's own instruments — the stable surface (gh#536)
Cache hit rate by series
panels.description: The share of cache-aside reads served without producing anything - the number R-1.1 and R-1.3 are judged on. A hit means the venue was not reached (bars) or nothing was projected (indicators, footprint). Falling towards zero on `bars` means the store is not retaining what it fetches; falling on `indicators` means something is re-projecting a series on every read.

panels.title: Cache reads by outcome
panels.description: The same counter, unrolled. `miss` is a cold series; `partial` is a series that grew, which is the ordinary state of a live instrument and is NOT a failing cache. A run of `miss` on a symbol that has already been read is the shape worth chasing.

panels.title: Venue calls by operation, and p95 duration
panels.description: One measurement per request actually issued to ProjectX, counted however it settled - a refused call spent the vendor allowance just as a successful one did. `get_bars` counts PAGES, not reads: the gateway pages at 1,000 bars and the pacer spaces the burst, so a cold year is legitimately around a hundred of these. Distinct from the HttpClient panel above, which cannot separate a venue call from this server's own OTLP export traffic.

panels.title: Gap fills by reason, and indicator values projected
panels.description: `absent` is a cold window, `gap` is a window the calendar expected more of, and `unattributed` is the gh#402/gh#412 heal re-asking for buckets that carry no contract id - that last one is a one-off migration cost and should trend to zero. Counted where the ranges are ASKED FOR, so a venue outage shows gap fills with no matching cache read. The projection series counts values a pass WROTE, so a confirming rebuild shows nothing at all: an empty diff is what makes indicators reproducible projections (ADR-0006).

panels.title: Tape: prints stored, hub transitions and claim hand-offs
panels.description: The only numbers there are for the market hub. Nothing instruments SignalR and the client package carries no activity source, so without these a silently dead subscription is indistinguishable from a quiet market (ADR-0016, gh#404). Ticks are counted where the print LANDED, past the coverage gate and the lease fence, so this agrees with the tape rather than with the hub. A `disconnected` with no matching `connected`, or a `lost` claim with no later `acquired`, is a recorder that has stopped recording.
